Article 208 When the People's Court receives a civil complaint submitted by a party, if the complaint meets the requirements of Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law and does not fall under the circumstances specified in Article 124, the court shall register the case and accept it; where it cannot be immediately determined whether the conditions for prosecution are met, the court shall accept the prosecution materials and issue a written receipt indicating the date of receipt.
Where necessary relevant materials need to be supplemented, the People's Court shall promptly inform the party. After the relevant materials are supplemented, the court shall decide whether to accept the case within seven days.
If after accepting the case it is discovered that the conditions for prosecution are not met or the case falls under the circumstances specified in Article 124 of the Civil Procedure Law, the court shall rule to dismiss the prosecution.

Article 209 Where the plaintiff provides the defendant's name or title, domicile and other information that is specific and clear, sufficient to distinguish the defendant from others, the defendant may be deemed as clearly identified.
Where the information on the defendant listed in the complaint is insufficient to identify a clear defendant, the People's Court may inform the plaintiff to make corrections. If after correction the plaintiff still cannot identify a clear defendant, the People's Court shall rule to not accept the case.
Article 210 Where the plaintiff's complaint contains abusive language and personal attacks, the People's Court shall inform the plaintiff to modify it before instituting an action.

Article 211 For a case over which this court has no jurisdiction, the plaintiff shall be informed to prosecute in the People's Court that has jurisdiction; where the plaintiff insists on prosecuting, the court shall rule to not accept the case; if after accepting the case it is discovered that this court has no jurisdiction, the case shall be transferred to the People's Court that has jurisdiction.

Article 212 In a case where a ruling has been made to not accept the case or to dismiss the prosecution, if the plaintiff prosecutes again and the prosecution meets the conditions for prosecution and does not fall under the circumstances specified in Article 124 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 213 Where the plaintiff is required to prepay the case acceptance fee but fails to do so, the People's Court shall notify the plaintiff to prepay it. If after such notification the plaintiff still fails to prepay it, or if an application for reduction, deferral, or exemption is not approved and the plaintiff still fails to prepay it, the court shall rule that the case be treated as withdrawn.

Article 214 After the plaintiff withdraws the lawsuit or the People's Court treats the case as withdrawn, if the plaintiff files another lawsuit based on the same claim, the People's Court shall accept the case.
For a divorce case where the plaintiff withdraws the lawsuit or the case is treated as withdrawn, if the plaintiff files another lawsuit within six months without new circumstances or new reasons, the case shall not be accepted by reference to the provisions of Article 124(7) of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 215 In accordance with Article 124(2) of the Civil Procedure Law, where the parties have included an arbitration clause in a written contract or have reached a written arbitration agreement after a dispute arises, and one party prosecutes in the People's Court, the People's Court shall inform the plaintiff to apply to an arbitration institution for arbitration; where the plaintiff insists on prosecuting, the court shall rule to not accept the case, except where the arbitration clause or arbitration agreement is not established, void, ceased to have effect, or its content is unclear and cannot be enforced.

Article 217 Where one spouse's whereabouts are unknown and the other spouse prosecutes in the People's Court, only seeking divorce and not applying for a declaration of disappearance or death of the missing person, the People's Court shall accept the case and shall serve litigation documents on the missing person by public notice.

Article 218 In cases concerning alimony, spousal support, or child support, after the judgment becomes legally effective, if a party prosecutes again to request an increase or reduction of the amount due to new circumstances or new reasons, the People's Court shall accept it as a new case.

Article 219 Where a party prosecutes after the limitation of action has expired, the People's Court shall accept the case. After acceptance, if the other party raises a defense based on the limitation of action, and the People's Court finds upon trial that the ground for defense is established, the court shall enter a judgment dismissing the plaintiff's claims.

Article 220 The term "trade secrets" as used in Articles 68, 134, and 156 of the Civil Procedure Law refers to technical secrets, business information, and data, such as production processes, formulas, trade connections, and purchase and sales channels, that the parties do not wish to be disclosed.
Article 221 Where a dispute arising from the same facts is prosecuted separately by the parties in the same People's Court, the People's Court may consolidate the trial.

Article 222 Where the plaintiff directly lists a third party in the statement of claim, it shall be deemed that the plaintiff applies to the People's Court for adding that third party to participate in the action. Whether to notify the third party to participate in the action shall be examined and decided by the People's Court.

Article 223 Where a party raises an objection to jurisdiction during the period for submitting the statement of defense and also responds to the content of the statement of claim, the People's Court shall, pursuant to Article 127, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, examine the objection to jurisdiction.
Where a party does not raise an objection to jurisdiction but submits a defense, makes statements, or files a counterclaim on the merits of the case, it may be deemed as the responsive defense as provided in Article 127, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 224 Pursuant to Article 133, Item 4 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court may, after the expiration of the period for submitting the statement of defense, make preparations before trial by organizing evidence exchange, convening a pre-trial conference, or other means.

Article 226 The People's Court shall, based on the parties' claims, defense opinions, and the status of evidence exchange, summarize the disputed issues and seek the parties' opinions on the summarized disputed issues.

Article 227 When a People's Court applies the ordinary procedure to try a case, it shall summon the parties by subpoena three days before the court session. It shall notify the litigation agents, witnesses, expert evaluators, inspectors, and interpreters to appear in court by notice. If the parties or other participants in the proceedings are in another location, necessary travel time shall be allowed.
Article 228 The court hearing shall focus on the key issues such as the disputed facts, evidence, and application of law.

Article 229 Where a party raises a different opinion during the court hearing regarding the facts and evidence admitted during the pre-trial preparation stage, the People's Court shall order the party to state reasons. When necessary, it may order the party to provide corresponding evidence. The People's Court shall conduct a review taking into account the parties' litigation capability, the evidence, and the specific circumstances of the case. If the reasons are established, they may be included in the disputed issues for trial.
Article 230 The People's Court may, based on the specific circumstances of the case and with the consent of the parties, conduct the court investigation and court debate jointly.

Article 231 Where a party presents new evidence in court, the People's Court shall handle it in accordance with Article 65, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law and the relevant provisions of this Interpretation.

Article 232 After the acceptance of the case and before the conclusion of the court debate, where the plaintiff adds claims, the defendant files a counterclaim, or a third party raises claims related to the case, and they may be consolidated for trial, the People's Court shall consolidate the trial.

Article 233 The parties to a counterclaim shall be limited to the scope of the parties to the original action.
Where the claims of the counterclaim and the original action are based on the same legal relationship, there is a causal relationship between the claims, or the claims of the counterclaim and the original action are based on the same facts, the People's Court shall consolidate the trial.
Where the counterclaim shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of another People's Court, or has no connection with the subject matter of the original action and the facts and reasons on which the claims of the original action are based, the People's Court shall issue a ruling to dismiss and inform the party to file a separate action.

Article 234 In a divorce action involving a person with no capacity for civil conduct, the legal representative of the party shall appear in court; if the legal representative cannot appear in court, the People's Court shall, on the basis of ascertaining the facts, render a judgment according to law.

Article 235 Where the legal representative of a party who has no capacity for civil conduct, after being summoned by subpoena, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, and if the legal representative belongs to the plaintiff's side, the case shall be treated as withdrawal of the action by analogy to Article 143 of the Civil Procedure Law; if the legal representative belongs to the defendant's side, a default judgment shall be rendered by analogy to Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law. When necessary, the People's Court may compel the legal representative to appear in court by a forcible summons.

Article 236 Where a third party with independent claims, after being summoned by subpoena by the People's Court, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or withdraws from court without the permission of the court, the case shall be treated as withdrawal of the action by analogy to Article 143 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 237 After a third party with independent claims participates in the action, if the plaintiff applies for withdrawal of the action, the People's Court, after granting the plaintiff's withdrawal, the third party with independent claims shall serve as the plaintiff in a separate case, and the original plaintiff and defendant shall serve as the defendants in the separate case, and the action shall continue.

Article 238 In a case where a party applies for withdrawal of the action or may be treated as withdrawal according to law, if the party has committed illegal acts that need to be dealt with according to law, the People's Court may refuse to grant the withdrawal or not treat the case as withdrawal.
After the conclusion of the court debate, if the plaintiff applies for withdrawal and the defendant does not consent, the People's Court may not grant the withdrawal.

Article 239 Where the People's Court grants the withdrawal of the original action by the plaintiff, it shall continue to try the counterclaim; if the defendant applies for withdrawal of the counterclaim, the People's Court shall grant it.

Article 240 Where a third party without independent claims, after being summoned by subpoena by the People's Court, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or withdraws from court without the permission of the court, it shall not affect the trial of the case.

Article 241: Where a defendant, having been summoned by service of a subpoena, refuses to appear before a court without justifiable grounds, or withdraws from a court session without permission of the court, the People's Court shall hold the court session as scheduled or continue to hold the court session for trial, and after hearing the claims of the party present, the arguments of both parties, and the evidence and other litigation materials already submitted, may make a default judgment according to law.

Article 242: After the pronouncement of a judgment at first instance, if the original trial People's Court discovers an error in the judgment and the party files an appeal within the appeal period, the original trial People's Court may submit its opinion that the original judgment is erroneous to the second instance People's Court, which shall try the case in accordance with the second instance procedure; if the party does not appeal, the matter shall be dealt with in accordance with the trial supervision procedure.

Article 243: The trial period as prescribed in Article 149 of the Civil Procedure Law means the period from the date on which a case is placed on file to the date on which a judgment or ruling is announced or a mediation agreement is served; provided that the period of public announcement, the period of expert evaluation, the period of conciliation between the parties, the period for hearing jurisdictional objections raised by the parties, and the period for handling jurisdictional disputes between People's Courts shall not be counted therein.

Article 244: Where a judgment or ruling that may be appealed against cannot be served on both parties simultaneously, the appeal period shall be calculated from the date on which each party receives the judgment or ruling.

Article 245: The clerical error as prescribed in Article 154, paragraph 1, item (7) of the Civil Procedure Law means erroneous writing or miscalculation in a legal instrument, omission or miscalculation of litigation costs, and other clerical errors.

Article 246: When the cause of a ruling to suspend the litigation is eliminated and the litigation procedure is resumed, it shall not be necessary to revoke the original ruling; the ruling to suspend the litigation shall cease to have effect from the time the People's Court notifies or permits both parties to continue the litigation.

Article 247: Where a party files another action on a matter for which an action has already been instituted, during the litigation process or after the judgment or ruling takes effect, and the following conditions are simultaneously satisfied, it shall constitute a duplicate action:
(1) the parties in the subsequent action and the prior action are identical;
(2) the subject matter of the subsequent action and that of the prior action are identical; and
(3) the claims of the subsequent action are identical to those of the prior action, or the claims of the subsequent action essentially negate the result of the prior judgment or ruling.
Where a party files a duplicate action, a ruling shall be made not to accept the case; if the case has already been accepted, a ruling shall be made to dismiss the action, unless otherwise provided by law or judicial interpretation.
Article 248: After a judgment or ruling becomes legally effective, if new facts occur and a party files an action again, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Article 249: During litigation, the transfer of the disputed civil rights and obligations shall not affect the party's status as a litigation subject or the party's position in the litigation. The legally effective judgment or ruling made by the People's Court shall be binding on the transferee.
If the transferee applies to participate in the action as a third party with no independent claim, the People's Court may grant permission. If the transferee applies to replace the party to assume the litigation, the People's Court may decide whether to grant permission based on the specific circumstances of the case; if permission is not granted, the transferee may be added as a third party with no independent claim.

Article 250: Where, in accordance with Article 249 of this Interpretation, the People's Court permits the transferee to replace the party to assume the litigation, a ruling shall be made to change the party.
After the party change, the litigation procedure shall continue with the transferee as the party, and the original party shall withdraw from the litigation. The procedural acts already completed by the original party shall be binding on the transferee.

Article 251: In a case where the second instance ruling sets aside the first instance judgment and remands the case for retrial, if the party applies to change or add claims or files a counterclaim, or if a third party files a claim related to the case, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 140 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 253: In a case where judgment is pronounced in court, except where the party requests at court that the judgment instrument be sent by mail, the People's Court shall inform the party or the litigation agent of the time and place for collecting the judgment instrument and the legal consequences of failure to collect it within the specified period. The above circumstances shall be recorded in the transcript.

Article 254: A citizen, legal person, or other organization that applies to inspect a legally effective judgment or ruling shall submit the application to the People's Court that rendered such effective judgment or ruling. The application shall be made in writing and shall provide the specific case number or the name of the party.

Article 256: 'Clearly established facts' in simple civil cases as prescribed in Article 157 of the Civil Procedure Law means that the parties' statements regarding the disputed facts are basically consistent and they can provide corresponding evidence, so the facts can be ascertained without the People's Court investigating and collecting evidence; 'clearly defined rights and obligations' means that it can be clearly distinguished who bears the liability and who enjoys the rights; and 'minor dispute' means that the parties have no fundamental disagreement regarding the merits of the case, the assumption of liability, and the subject matter of the action.

Article 258: If a case tried under the summary procedure, upon expiry of the trial period, both parties agree to continue applying the summary procedure, the trial period may be extended with the approval of the president of this court. The cumulative trial period after extension shall not exceed six months.
If the People's Court finds that the case is complex and needs to be tried under the ordinary procedure, it shall make a ruling before the expiry of the trial period and notify both parties in writing of the composition of the collegial panel and related matters.
If the case is converted to be tried under the ordinary procedure, the trial period shall be calculated from the date on which the People's Court places the case on file.

Article 259: Both parties may submit an application to the People's Court regarding the method of holding a court session, and the People's Court shall decide whether to grant permission. With the consent of both parties, the court session may be conducted by means of audiovisual transmission technology or other means.
Article 260: A case that has already been tried under the ordinary procedure shall not be converted to trial under the summary procedure after the court session has been held.

第二百六十一条 For cases tried under the summary procedure, the People's Court may summon the parties, notify witnesses, and serve procedural documents other than adjudicative documents by such simple means as sending verbal messages, telephone, text messages, facsimile, or email.
Where the notice of a court session is served by simple means, the People's Court shall not render a default judgment if it has not been confirmed by the parties or there is no other evidence proving that the parties have received it.
A case tried under the summary procedure shall be tried by a single judge alone, with a court clerk keeping the record.

第二百六十二条 The judgments, rulings, and mediation documents prepared by a People's Tribunal must be affixed with the seal of the Primary People's Court, and the seal of the People's Tribunal shall not be used in substitution for the seal of the Primary People's Court.

第二百六十四条 Where the parties agree to apply the summary procedure in accordance with the provisions of Article 157, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law, they shall submit such request before the court session. If the request is made orally, it shall be recorded in the record and confirmed by the signatures or thumbprints of both parties.
For cases specified in Article 257 of this Interpretation, if the parties agree to apply the summary procedure, the People's Court shall not permit it.

第二百六十五条 Where the plaintiff brings an oral complaint, the People's Court shall accurately record in the record the basic information of the parties such as name, gender, work unit, domicile, and contact information, the claim, the facts and reasons, and the plaintiff shall sign or thumbprint after verifying that it is correct. A receipt shall be issued for the evidentiary materials submitted by the parties.

第二百六十六条 The time limit for adducing evidence in a case applying the summary procedure shall be determined by the People's Court, or may be agreed upon by the parties through consultation and permitted by the People's Court, provided that it shall not exceed fifteen days. Where the defendant requests a written defense, the People's Court may, on the basis of obtaining the defendant's consent, reasonably determine the period for defense.
The People's Court shall inform both parties of the time limit for adducing evidence and the date of the court session, and shall explain to the parties the legal consequences of failure to adduce evidence within the time limit and failure to appear in court, and both parties shall sign or thumbprint on the record and the receipt of service of the summons.
Where both parties indicate that they do not need a time limit for adducing evidence or a period for defense, the People's Court may immediately try the case or determine the date of the court session.
第二百六十七条 In a case tried under the summary procedure, preparations before trial may be conducted in a simple manner.

第二百六十八条 For a party who has not retained a lawyer or a basic legal service worker to act as agent in the action, the People's Court may, during the court proceedings, give necessary explanations or clarifications to the party concerning such relevant matters as withdrawal, admission, and burden of proof, and shall, during the court proceedings, appropriately remind the party to correctly exercise procedural rights and perform procedural obligations.

第二百六十九条 Where a party raises an objection to the application of the summary procedure to the case, and the People's Court, upon examination, finds that the objection is sustainable, it shall rule to convert the case to the ordinary procedure; if the objection is not sustainable, it shall orally inform the party and record it in the record.
Where the case is converted to the ordinary procedure, the People's Court shall notify both parties in writing of the composition of the collegiate bench and other relevant matters.
Before the conversion to the ordinary procedure, facts that have been confirmed by both parties may be exempted from further adducing evidence and cross-examination.
第二百七十一十一条 The People's Court shall, when trying a small claims case, apply the provisions of Article 162 of the Civil Procedure Law and implement a final instance of first instance.

第二百七十二 The average annual wage of employed persons in the previous year of each province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government as specified in Article 162 of the Civil Procedure Law means the average annual wage of employed persons of the previous year already published for each province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. Before the publication of the average annual wage of employed persons of the previous year, the average annual wage of employed persons of the most recent year already published shall prevail.

第二百七十三 A maritime court may try small claims cases concerning maritime and commercial maritime matters. The amount in controversy of the case shall be limited to thirty percent of the average annual wage of employed persons in the previous year of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the maritime court that actually accepts the case or its field tribunal is located.

第二百七十六 The People's Court, when accepting a small claims case, shall inform the parties of relevant matters such as the adjudication organ for such cases, the final instance of first instance, the trial period, and the standard for payment of litigation costs.

第二百七十七 The time limit for adducing evidence in a small claims case shall be determined by the People's Court, or may be agreed upon by the parties through consultation and permitted by the People's Court, but generally shall not exceed seven days.
Where the defendant requests a written defense, the People's Court may, on the basis of obtaining the defendant's consent, reasonably determine the period for defense, but the maximum period shall not exceed fifteen days.
Where the parties, after appearing in court, indicate that they do not need a time limit for adducing evidence or a period for defense, the People's Court may immediately try the case.
第二百七十八 Where a party raises an objection to jurisdiction over a small claims case, the People's Court shall render a ruling. The ruling shall take effect as soon as it is rendered.

第二百七十九 Where, after accepting a small claims case, the People's Court finds that the prosecution does not meet the conditions for prosecution prescribed in Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall rule to dismiss the prosecution. The ruling shall take effect as soon as it is rendered.

第二百八十 Where, due to the party's application to increase or change the claim, file a counterclaim, join additional parties, or other reasons, the case no longer meets the conditions for a small claims case, the other provisions on the summary procedure shall apply to the trial.
For a case as prescribed in the preceding paragraph that should be tried under the ordinary procedure, the case shall be converted to the ordinary procedure by ruling.
Before the trial under the other provisions on the summary procedure or the ordinary procedure, facts that have been confirmed by both parties may be exempted from further adducing evidence and cross-examination.

Article 281 If a party objects to the trial of a case as a small claims case, the objection shall be raised before the court session. After examination by the People's Court, if the objection is sustained, the case shall be tried under other provisions of the summary procedure; if the objection is not sustained, the party shall be informed and the matter shall be recorded in the transcript.
Article 282 The judgment or ruling documents for small claims cases may be simplified, mainly containing the basic information of the parties, the claims, and the main text of the judgment or ruling.
Article 283 Where the People's Court tries a small claims case, if this Interpretation has no provisions, other provisions of the summary procedure shall apply.

Article 285 A public interest action shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intermediate People's Court of the place where the tortious act occurred or where the defendant is domiciled, unless otherwise provided by laws or judicial interpretations.
A public interest action initiated for pollution of the marine environment shall be under the jurisdiction of the maritime court of the place where the pollution occurred, the place where the damage occurred, or the place where preventive measures were taken.
Where public interest actions are initiated separately in two or more People's Courts for the same tortious act, the People's Court that first docketed the case shall have jurisdiction; if necessary, the common superior People's Court of those courts shall designate jurisdiction.
Article 286 After accepting a public interest action, the People's Court shall, within ten days, notify in writing the relevant administrative department.

Article 287 After the People's Court accepts a public interest action, other authorities and relevant organizations that may initiate an action according to law may apply to the People's Court to participate in the action before the court session. If the People's Court grants permission to participate, they shall be listed as co-plaintiffs.

Article 288 The acceptance of a public interest action by the People's Court shall not affect the right of a victim of the same tortious act to initiate an action under Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 289 In a public interest action, the parties may reach a settlement, and the People's Court may conduct mediation.
After the parties reach a settlement or mediation agreement, the People's Court shall make a public announcement of the settlement or mediation agreement. The period for public announcement shall not be less than thirty days.
After the expiration of the public announcement period, if the People's Court, upon examination, finds that the settlement or mediation agreement does not violate the public interest, it shall issue a mediation paper; if the settlement or mediation agreement violates the public interest, it shall not issue a mediation paper and shall continue to try the case and render a judgment according to law.
Article 290 If the plaintiff in a public interest action applies for withdrawal of the action after the conclusion of court debate, the People's Court shall not grant permission.

Article 291 After the judgment or ruling in a public interest action becomes legally effective, if another authority or relevant organization that has standing as a plaintiff according to law initiates another public interest action for the same tortious act, the People's Court shall rule that the action shall not be accepted, unless otherwise provided by laws or judicial interpretations.

Article 293 The People's Court shall, within five days from the date of receiving the complaint and evidence materials, serve them on the opposing party, and the opposing party may submit written opinions within ten days from the date of receiving the complaint.
The People's Court shall examine the complaint, evidence materials submitted by the third party, and the written opinions of the opposing party. If necessary, the People's Court may question both parties.
Upon examination, if the conditions for prosecution are met, the People's Court shall docket the case within thirty days from the date of receiving the complaint. If the conditions for prosecution are not met, the People's Court shall rule within thirty days from the date of receiving the complaint that the action shall not be accepted.
Article 294 The People's Court shall form a collegial panel and hold a court session to try a case involving a third-party action to set aside a judgment, ruling, or mediation paper.

Article 296 "The whole or part of the content" of a judgment, ruling, or mediation paper as provided in paragraph 3 of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law refers to the main text of the judgment or ruling, and the result of disposing of the parties' civil rights and obligations in the mediation paper.

Article 298 Where a third party initiates an action to set aside a judgment, ruling, or mediation paper, the People's Court shall list the third party as the plaintiff, the parties to the effective judgment, ruling, or mediation paper as the defendants, except that a third party without independent claims who bears no liability in the effective judgment, ruling, or mediation paper shall be listed as a third party.

Article 299 After accepting a case of a third-party action to set aside a judgment, ruling, or mediation paper, if the plaintiff provides appropriate security and requests a stay of enforcement, the People's Court may grant permission.

Article 301 During the period of trial of a third party revocation action, if the People's Court decides to retry an effective judgment, ruling, or mediation statement, the People's Court that accepted the third party revocation action shall rule to incorporate the third party's claims into the retrial procedure. However, if there is evidence proving that the original parties colluded maliciously to harm the third party's lawful rights and interests, the People's Court shall first hear the third party revocation action case and rule to suspend the retrial proceedings.

Article 303 After a third party files a revocation action, if the execution of the effective judgment, ruling, or mediation statement is not suspended, the executing court shall review the execution objection raised by the third party in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. If the third party is dissatisfied with the ruling rejecting the execution objection and applies for retrial of the original judgment, ruling, or mediation statement, the People's Court shall not accept it.
If a person not involved in the case is dissatisfied with the People's Court's ruling rejecting his/her execution objection and believes that the content of the original judgment, ruling, or mediation statement is erroneous and damages his/her lawful rights and interests, he/she shall apply for retrial in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; if he/she files a third party revocation action, the People's Court shall not accept it.

Article 304 According to Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, where a person not involved in the case or a party, dissatisfied with the ruling on the execution objection, initiates an execution objection lawsuit within fifteen days from the date of service of the ruling, such lawsuit shall be under the jurisdiction of the executing court.

Article 307 Where a person not involved in the case initiates an execution objection lawsuit, the enforcement applicant shall be the defendant. If the person subject to enforcement objects to the objection of the person not involved in the case, the person subject to enforcement shall be a co-defendant; if the person subject to enforcement does not object, the person subject to enforcement may be listed as a third party.

Article 308 Where the enforcement applicant initiates an execution objection lawsuit, the person not involved in the case shall be the defendant. If the person subject to enforcement objects to the claim of the enforcement applicant, the person not involved in the case and the person subject to enforcement shall be co-defendants; if the person subject to enforcement does not object, the person subject to enforcement may be listed as a third party.

Article 309 If the enforcement applicant does not initiate an execution objection lawsuit against the ruling to suspend execution, and the person subject to enforcement initiates an execution objection lawsuit, the People's Court shall inform the person subject to enforcement to file a separate lawsuit.
Article 310 The People's Court shall apply the ordinary procedure when trying execution objection lawsuit cases.

Article 311 Where a person not involved in the case or the enforcement applicant initiates an execution objection lawsuit, the person not involved in the case shall bear the burden of proof to demonstrate that he/she has a civil right or interest in the subject matter of execution sufficient to exclude compulsory execution.

Article 312 For an execution objection lawsuit initiated by a person not involved in the case, after trial, the People's Court shall treat it separately according to the following circumstances:
(1) If the person not involved in the case has a civil right or interest in the subject matter of execution sufficient to exclude compulsory execution, it shall render a judgment that the subject matter of execution shall not be executed;
(2) If the person not involved in the case does not have a civil right or interest in the subject matter of execution sufficient to exclude compulsory execution, it shall render a judgment rejecting the claims.
If the person not involved in the case simultaneously raises a claim for confirmation of his/her right, the People's Court may make a ruling together in the judgment.

Article 314 For an execution objection lawsuit of a person not involved in the case, if the People's Court renders a judgment that the subject matter of execution shall not be executed, the ruling on execution objection shall cease to be effective.
For an execution objection lawsuit of the enforcement applicant, if the People's Court renders a judgment permitting execution of the subject matter of execution, the ruling on execution objection shall cease to be effective, and the executing court may resume execution upon the application of the enforcement applicant or ex officio.

Article 315 During the trial of an execution objection lawsuit of a person not involved in the case, the People's Court shall not dispose of the subject matter of execution. If the enforcement applicant requests the People's Court to continue execution and provides corresponding security, the People's Court may permit it.
If the person subject to enforcement and the person not involved in the case collude maliciously to hinder execution through an execution objection or an execution objection lawsuit, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 113 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. If the enforcement applicant suffers damage as a result, he/she may initiate a lawsuit to claim compensation from the person subject to enforcement and the person not involved in the case.

Article 316 After the People's Court rules to suspend execution of the subject matter of execution, if the enforcement applicant does not initiate an execution objection lawsuit within the period prescribed by law, the People's Court shall, within seven days from the date of expiration of the limitation for prosecution, lift the enforcement measures taken against the subject matter of execution.

Article 317 If both parties and the third party all appeal, all of them shall be listed as appellants. The People's Court may determine the litigation status of the parties in the second instance procedure ex officio.
Article 318 The counterparty provided for in Articles 166 and 167 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China shall include the respondent and other parties in the original trial.

Article 320 At the time of pronouncement of the first instance judgment or service of the judgment or ruling, if a party orally expresses an intention to appeal, the People's Court shall inform the party that he/she must submit a written appeal within the statutory appeal period. If the written appeal is not submitted within the statutory appeal period, it shall be deemed that no appeal has been filed. If a written appeal is submitted but the appeal fee is not paid within the specified time limit, it shall be treated as automatic withdrawal of the appeal.
The legal representative of a person with no or limited capacity for civil conduct may file an appeal on behalf of the party.

Where a party to an appeal case dies or is terminated, the People's Court shall, according to law, notify the successor of its rights and obligations to participate in the proceedings.
If the litigation needs to be terminated, Article 151 of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply.

The People's Court of second instance shall conduct adjudication focusing on the appeal claims of the parties.
Claims not raised by the parties shall not be adjudicated, unless the first-instance judgment violates prohibitive provisions of law, or damages the national interest, social public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others.
For appeal cases tried in court sessions, the People's Court of second instance may, pursuant to Article 133(4) of the Civil Procedure Law, conduct preparations before adjudication.

Where the original trial People's Court did not adjudicate or render judgment on a claim already raised by a party in the first-instance proceedings, the People's Court of second instance may conduct mediation based on the principle of voluntariness of the parties; if mediation fails, the case shall be remanded for retrial.

Where a party who must participate in the litigation or a third party with independent claims did not participate in the first-instance proceedings, the People's Court of second instance may conduct mediation based on the principle of voluntariness of the parties; if mediation fails, the case shall be remanded for retrial.

In the second-instance proceedings, if the original plaintiff adds an independent claim or the original defendant files a counterclaim, the People's Court of second instance may, based on the principle of voluntariness of the parties, conduct mediation on the newly added claim or counterclaim; if mediation fails, the parties shall be informed to file a separate lawsuit.
If both parties agree to have the People's Court of second instance adjudicate together, the People's Court of second instance may render a judgment together.

In a case where the first-instance judgment does not grant divorce, after appeal, if the People's Court of second instance considers that divorce shall be granted, it may, based on the principle of voluntariness of the parties, conduct mediation together with issues of child custody and property; if mediation fails, the case shall be remanded for retrial.
If both parties agree to have the People's Court of second instance adjudicate together, the People's Court of second instance may render a judgment together.

Where a People's Court hearing a case under second-instance procedures considers that the case should not have been accepted by a People's Court according to law, the People's Court of second instance may directly rule to revoke the original judgment and dismiss the prosecution.

Where a People's Court hearing a case under second-instance procedures considers that the first-instance People's Court accepted the case in violation of exclusive jurisdiction provisions, it shall rule to revoke the original judgment and transfer the case to a People's Court with jurisdiction.

If the People's Court of second instance ascertains that the ruling of non-acceptance made by the first-instance People's Court is erroneous, it shall, while revoking the original ruling, instruct the first-instance People's Court to docket and accept the case; if it ascertains that the ruling to dismiss the prosecution made by the first-instance People's Court is erroneous, it shall, while revoking the original ruling, instruct the first-instance People's Court to adjudicate.

If the original judgment or ruling has defects in fact-finding or application of law, but the result of the adjudication is correct, the People's Court of second instance may, after correcting the defects in the judgment or ruling, uphold it in accordance with Article 170(1)(1) of the Civil Procedure Law.

The basic facts referred to in Article 170(1)(3) of the Civil Procedure Law mean facts used to determine the party's qualification, the nature of the case, civil rights and obligations, etc., which have a substantive impact on the results of the original judgment or ruling.

In the second-instance proceedings, if a legal person or other organization that is a party divides, the People's Court may directly list the divided legal persons or other organizations as co-litigants; if they merge, the merged legal person or other organization shall be listed as a party.

In the second-instance proceedings, if a party applies to withdraw an appeal, and upon review the People's Court considers that the first-instance judgment is indeed erroneous, or that the parties have maliciously colluded to damage the national interest, social public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others, the application shall not be granted.

In the second-instance proceedings, if the original plaintiff applies to withdraw the prosecution, with the consent of the other parties and without damaging the national interest, social public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others, the People's Court may grant the application. If withdrawal is granted, a ruling shall be made simultaneously to revoke the first-instance judgment.
If the original plaintiff, after withdrawing the prosecution in the second-instance proceedings, files a duplicate prosecution, the People's Court shall not accept it.

Where the parties reach a settlement agreement in the second-instance proceedings, the People's Court may, upon the request of the parties, review the settlement agreement reached by the parties and prepare a mediation document to be served on the parties; if an application for withdrawal of the action is filed due to the settlement, and upon review it meets the conditions for withdrawal, the People's Court shall grant it.

The People's Court of second instance may pronounce the judgment by itself, or may entrust the original trial People's Court or the People's Court at the place of the parties to pronounce the judgment on its behalf.

Article 341 When a People's Court hears an appeal case against a ruling, it shall make a final ruling within thirty days from the date of filing the appeal for second instance. Where special circumstances require an extension of the trial period, approval shall be obtained from the president of the court.

Article 342 The litigation acts performed by a party in the first instance proceedings shall remain binding on that party in the second instance proceedings.
Where a party repudiates the litigation acts performed in the first instance proceedings, the People's Court shall order it to state the reasons therefor. Where the reasons are not established, they shall not be upheld.

Article 343 In a case of declaring a person missing or dead, the People's Court may, upon the request of the applicant, sort out the property of the missing person and appoint a property manager during the trial period. After the expiration of the public notice period, if the People's Court renders a judgment declaring the person missing, it shall, at the same time, appoint a property custodian for the missing person in accordance with Article 42 of the Civil Code.

Article 344 After a property custodian for a missing person is designated by the People's Court, if the custodian applies for a change of custodian, the case shall be heard by reference to the relevant provisions of the Special Procedure in the Civil Procedure Law. Where the reasons for the application are established, a ruling shall be made to revoke the applicant's status as custodian and simultaneously designate another property custodian; where the reasons for the application are not established, the application shall be rejected by a ruling.
Where any other interested person of the missing person applies for a change of custodian, the People's Court shall inform it to file a lawsuit against the originally designated custodian, and the case shall be heard in accordance with the ordinary procedure.

Article 345 After a People's Court renders a judgment declaring a citizen missing, if an interested person applies to the People's Court for declaring the missing person dead, and four full years have elapsed since the date of disappearance, the People's Court shall accept the case. The judgment declaring the person missing shall serve as proof of the citizen's disappearance, and during the trial, a public notice shall still be given in accordance with Article 185 of the Civil Procedure Law.
Article 346 Where multiple interested persons who meet the legal requirements file applications for declaring a person missing or dead, they shall be listed as joint applicants.

Article 348 After a People's Court accepts a case of declaring a person missing or dead, and before rendering a judgment, if the applicant withdraws the application, the People's Court shall make a ruling to terminate the case, except where other interested persons who meet the legal requirements join the proceedings and request to continue the trial.

Article 349 During the litigation, if an interested person of a party claims that the party suffers from a mental disorder and requests a declaration that the party has no capacity or has limited capacity for civil conduct, the interested person shall file an application with the People's Court, and the court accepting the original action shall institute the case and hear it in accordance with the special procedure, and the original litigation shall be suspended.

Article 350 In a case of determining property as ownerless, if during the period of public notice a person makes a claim on the property, the People's Court shall make a ruling to terminate the special procedure, and shall inform the applicant to file a separate lawsuit, which shall be heard in accordance with the ordinary procedure.

Article 351 Where the designated guardian disagrees with the designation by the residents' committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department, it shall file an objection with the People's Court within thirty days from the date of receiving the notice. Upon trial, if it is found that the designation is not improper, a ruling shall be made to reject the objection; if the designation is improper, a judgment shall be made to revoke the designation and simultaneously designate another guardian. The judgment shall be served on the objector, the original designating entity, and the guardian designated in the judgment.
Where a relevant party directly applies to the People's Court for designating a guardian in accordance with Article 31, paragraph 1 of the Civil Code, the case shall be heard in accordance with the special procedure, and a judgment shall be made to designate a guardian. The judgment shall be served on the applicant and the guardian designated in the judgment.

Article 352 In a case of applying for determining a citizen as having no capacity or limited capacity for civil conduct, if the respondent has no close relatives, the People's Court may designate an individual or organization that is willing to act as agent and is approved by the residents' committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department of the respondent's domicile as the agent.
Where there is no agent as provided in the preceding paragraph, the residents' committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department of the respondent's domicile shall act as the agent.
The agent may be one person, or two persons in the same order.

Article 353 When applying for judicial confirmation of a mediation agreement, both parties shall submit the application in person or through an agent ad litem that meets the requirements of Article 58 of the Civil Procedure Law, to the primary people's court or people's tribunal at the place where the mediation organization is located.

Article 354 Where two or more mediation organizations participate in mediation, each primary people's court at the place where the respective mediation organization is located shall have jurisdiction.
The parties may jointly submit the application to one primary people's court at the place where a mediation organization is located; where the parties jointly submit the application to two or more primary people's courts at the places where mediation organizations are located, the court that first dockets the case shall have jurisdiction.

Article 355 A party applying for judicial confirmation of a mediation agreement may do so in writing or orally. Where a party makes an oral application, the People's Court shall record it in the transcripts, and the party shall sign, affix its thumbprint, or seal the transcripts.

Article 356 When applying for judicial confirmation of a mediation agreement, a party shall submit to the People's Court the mediation agreement, the certificate that the mediation was conducted under the auspices of the mediation organization, and the documents relating to property rights related to the mediation agreement, and shall provide basic information such as the identities, domiciles, and contact methods of both parties.
Where the party fails to submit the above materials, the People's Court shall request the party to supplement them within a specified period.

Article 358 When reviewing the relevant circumstances, the People's Court shall notify both parties to be present together to verify the case.
If, upon review, the People's Court considers that the statements of the parties or the supporting materials provided are insufficient, incomplete, or questionable, it may request the parties to supplement their statements or supplementary supporting materials within a specified period. When necessary, the People's Court may verify the relevant information with the mediation organization.

Article 359 Before a ruling confirming the mediation agreement is made, if a party withdraws the application, the People's Court may grant permission by a ruling.
Where a party, without justifiable reasons, fails to supplement statements or supplementary supporting materials within the specified period, or refuses to accept an inquiry, the People's Court may treat the matter as a withdrawal of the application.

Article 361 The security interest holders as specified in Article 196 of the Civil Procedure Law shall include mortgagees, pledgees, and lienholders; other persons entitled to request the realization of security interests shall include mortgagors, pledgors, the debtor whose property is under lien, or owners, etc.

Article 362 Cases on the realization of a pledge of rights with documents of title, such as negotiable instruments, warehouse receipts, and bills of lading, may be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of domicile of the holder of the documents of title; where the pledge of rights is without such documents, it shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of the pledge registration.

Article 363 Where a case on the realization of a security interest falls under the jurisdiction of a specialized People's Court, such as a maritime court, it shall be under the jurisdiction of the specialized People's Court.

Article 364 Where there are multiple secured properties for the same creditor's right and their locations differ, and the applicant applies separately to the People's Courts having jurisdiction for the realization of the security interest, the People's Courts shall accept the applications according to law.

Article 365 In accordance with Article 392 of the Civil Code, where the secured claim is guaranteed by both a property security and a personal security, and the parties have agreed on the order of realizing the security interests, if the application for realizing the security interest violates such agreement, the People's Court shall rule to reject the application; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the People's Court shall accept the application.

Article 366 Where multiple security interests are established on the same property, if a prior registered security interest has not yet been realized, it shall not affect the right of a subsequent-ranking security interest holder to apply to the People's Court for the realization of the security interest.

Article 368 After accepting the application, the People's Court shall, within five days, serve upon the respondent the copy of the application, the notice of the right to raise an objection, and other documents.
If the respondent has any objection, it shall raise it with the People's Court within five days after receiving the notice from the People's Court, and shall simultaneously state the reasons and provide corresponding evidence.

Article 369 A case on the realization of a security interest may be reviewed by a single judge. If the amount of the object of the secured property exceeds the jurisdiction of a Primary People's Court, a collegial panel shall be formed for review.

Article 370 When reviewing a case on the realization of a security interest, the People's Court may inquire of the applicant, the respondent, and interested persons, and may, when necessary, investigate relevant facts ex officio.

Article 371 The People's Court shall review the validity, term, and performance of the principal contract, whether the security interest has been validly established, the scope of the secured property, the scope of the secured claim, whether the secured claim has become due (i.e., the conditions for realizing the security interest), and whether it infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of others.
If the respondent or an interested person raises an objection, the People's Court shall review it concurrently.

Article 373 After the People's Court has accepted the application, if the applicant applies for preservation of the secured property, the matter may be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on preservation in litigation.

Article 374 With respect to judgments and rulings rendered under the special procedure, if a party or an interested person considers them erroneous, it may raise an objection to the People's Court that rendered the judgment or ruling. Upon review, if the objection is sustained or partially sustained, the People's Court shall render a new judgment or ruling to revoke or modify the original judgment or ruling; if the objection is not sustained, it shall rule to reject the objection.
With respect to a ruling of the People's Court confirming a mediation agreement or permitting the realization of a security interest, if a party has an objection, it shall be raised within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the ruling; if an interested person has an objection, it shall be raised within six months from the date when it knows or should have known that its civil rights and interests are infringed.

Article 375 If a party dies or terminates, the successor to its rights and obligations may apply for retrial in accordance with Article 199 and Article 201 of the Civil Procedure Law.
After a judgment or mediation statement takes effect, if a party assigns the claim confirmed by the judgment or mediation statement, and the assignee of the claim, dissatisfied with the judgment or mediation statement, applies for retrial, the People's Court shall not accept the application.

Article 376 The phrase "a large number of parties on one side" as provided in Article 199 of the Civil Procedure Law shall include citizens, legal persons, and other organizations.
The case referred to in Article 199 of the Civil Procedure Law where both parties to the case are citizens shall mean a case in which both the plaintiff and the defendant are citizens.

Article 379 In a case where one party is composed of a large number of persons, or both parties are citizens, if the parties separately apply for retrial to the original trial People's Court and the People's Court at the next higher level and cannot reach an agreement, the original trial People's Court shall accept the application.

Article 380 In cases heard under non-contentious procedures such as the special procedure, the summary procedure, the public summons procedure, the bankruptcy procedure, etc., the parties shall not apply for retrial.
Article 381 If a party considers that a legally effective ruling on rejection of acceptance or dismissal of a lawsuit is erroneous, it may apply for a retrial.

Article 382 Where a party applies for retrial on the issue of property division in a divorce case, if it involves property already divided in the judgment, the People's Court shall conduct review in accordance with Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law; if the conditions for retrial are met, it shall rule for retrial; if it involves community property not dealt with in the judgment, it shall inform the party to file a separate action.
Article 384 A party applying for retrial against a legally effective mediation agreement shall file the application within six months after the mediation agreement takes legal effect.

Article 385 The People's Court shall, within five days from the date of receiving the qualified application for retrial and other materials, send a notice of acceptance to the applicant for retrial, and send a notice of response, a copy of the application for retrial, and other materials to the respondent and other parties of the original trial.

Article 386 After accepting a case of application for retrial, the People's Court shall review the grounds for retrial claimed by the party in accordance with the provisions of Articles 200, 201, and 204 of the Civil Procedure Law and other provisions.

Article 387 Where new evidence provided by the applicant for retrial can prove that the basic facts determined or the adjudication result of the original judgment or ruling is erroneous, it shall be found as the circumstance specified in Item (1) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law.
For evidence that meets the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the People's Court shall order the applicant for retrial to explain the reasons for its late submission; if the applicant refuses to explain the reasons or the reasons are not established, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 65 of the Civil Procedure Law and Article 102 of this Interpretation.

Article 389 Where a party, in the original trial, refused to express an opinion on cross-examination of the main evidence for the facts determined by the original judgment or ruling, or did not express an opinion on cross-examination of the evidence during cross-examination, it shall not fall under the circumstance of 'without cross-examination' as specified in Item (4) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 392 The claims for relief as specified in Item (11) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law include the claims of the first instance and the claims on appeal of the second instance, except where the party did not appeal against the omission of a claim or a claim exceeding the scope of claims in the first instance judgment or ruling.

Article 394 The conduct of adjudicators as specified in Item (13) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, such as embezzlement, bribery, favoritism, and perversion of the law in adjudication, refers to conduct that has been confirmed by an effective criminal legal instrument or a decision on disciplinary sanction.

Article 395 Where the grounds for retrial claimed by a party are established and the conditions for applying for retrial under the Civil Procedure Law and this Interpretation are met, the People's Court shall rule for retrial.
Where the grounds for retrial claimed by a party are not established, or the party's application for retrial exceeds the statutory time limit for applying for retrial or exceeds the scope of statutory grounds for retrial, and thus does not meet the conditions for applying for retrial under the Civil Procedure Law and this Interpretation, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the application for retrial.

Article 396 Where the People's Court decides on its own to retry a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement according to law, and it is necessary to suspend enforcement in accordance with the provisions of Article 206 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall simultaneously specify in the retrial ruling the suspension of enforcement of the original judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement; in an emergency, the People's Court may orally notify the People's Court responsible for enforcement of the ruling to suspend enforcement, and shall issue a written ruling within ten days after the notification.

Article 397 The People's Court decides whether to question the parties based on the needs of reviewing the case. Where new evidence may overturn the original judgment or ruling, the People's Court shall question the parties.

Article 398 During the review of an application for retrial, if the respondent and other parties of the original trial submit an application for retrial according to law, the People's Court shall list them as applicants for retrial, review their grounds for retrial together, and the review period shall be recalculated. Upon review, if the grounds for retrial claimed by one of the applicants for retrial are established, it shall rule for retrial. If the grounds for retrial claimed by all the applicants for retrial are not established, it shall rule to dismiss all the applications for retrial.

Article 399 During the review of an application for retrial, if the applicant for retrial applies to the People's Court to commission an expert evaluation or inspection, the People's Court shall not permit it.

Article 400 During the review of an application for retrial, whether to permit the withdrawal of the application for retrial by the applicant for retrial shall be decided by the People's Court.
Where the applicant for retrial, having been summoned by a summons, refuses without justifiable reasons to accept questioning, it may be treated as withdrawal of the application for retrial.

Article 401 Where the People's Court permits the withdrawal of a retrial application or the case is treated as withdrawal of the retrial application, and the retrial applicant files another retrial application, it shall not be accepted unless there are circumstances as provided in Items (1), (3), (12), and (13) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law and the application is filed within six months from the date the applicant knew or should have known thereof.

Article 403 In trying a retrial case, the People's Court shall form a collegial panel and hold a hearing, except where the case is tried under the second instance procedure and there are special circumstances, or both parties have fully expressed their opinions through other means and agree in writing not to hold a hearing.
If the conditions for a default judgment are met, a default judgment may be rendered.

Article 405 In trying a retrial case, the People's Court shall focus on the retrial request. Where the party's retrial request exceeds the original claims, it shall not be tried; where it meets the conditions for a separate action, the parties shall be informed that they may file a separate action.
Where the respondent or other original trial parties raise a retrial request before the conclusion of the court debate and such request conforms to the provisions of Article 205 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall try all such requests together.
If, during the retrial, the People's Court finds that the legally effective judgment or ruling infringes upon the national interests, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others, it shall try all such matters together.

Article 407 If the People's Court, after retrial, considers that the original judgment or ruling has clear findings of fact and correct application of law, it shall be affirmed. If the original judgment or ruling has defects in the finding of fact or application of law but the adjudicative result is correct, the defects shall be corrected in the retrial judgment or ruling, and then the judgment or ruling shall be affirmed.
If the original judgment or ruling has errors in the finding of fact or application of law, resulting in an incorrect adjudicative result, it shall be modified, revoked, or changed according to law.

Article 408 For a case retried under the second instance procedure, if the People's Court, after trial, finds that the conditions for prosecution prescribed by the Civil Procedure Law are not met or the case falls under the circumstances for non-acceptance as provided in Article 124 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall rule to revoke the judgments of first and second instance and dismiss the prosecution.

Article 409 After a People's Court rules to retry a mediation document, it shall handle the case according to the following circumstances:
(1) If the ground raised by the party that the mediation violated the principle of voluntariness is not established and the content of the mediation document does not violate the mandatory provisions of law, a ruling shall be made to reject the retrial application;
(2) If the ground asserted by the People's Procuratorate in the protest or the retrial procuratorial suggestion that the mediation document harmed national interests or social public interests is not established, a ruling shall be made to terminate the retrial procedure.
Under the circumstances of the preceding paragraph, if the mediation document for which enforcement was suspended by the People's Court's ruling needs to continue enforcement, the enforcement shall automatically resume.

Article 410 If, during the retrial proceedings, the first-instance plaintiff applies to withdraw the prosecution, and with the consent of the other parties and without harming national interests, social public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others, the People's Court may permit it. Where the ruling permits the withdrawal, the original judgment shall be revoked simultaneously.
If the first-instance plaintiff files a repeated prosecution after withdrawing the prosecution in the retrial proceedings, the People's Court shall not accept it.

Article 411 If, due to the submission of new evidence by a party, the original judgment is modified upon retrial, and the failure to timely produce evidence in the original trial procedure was caused by the fault of the retrial applicant or the party applying for procuratorial supervision, and the respondent or other parties request compensation for the necessary expenses such as transportation, accommodation, meals, and loss of working time, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 412 If some of the parties appear in court and reach a mediation agreement, and the other parties have not made any written expression, the People's Court shall state that fact in the judgment; if the content of the mediation agreement does not violate the provisions of law and does not harm the lawful rights and interests of the other parties, it may be confirmed in the main text of the judgment.

Article 413 Where the People's Procuratorate, according to law, files a protest against a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document that harms national interests or social public interests, or issues a retrial procuratorial suggestion after deliberation and decision by the procuratorial committee of the People's Procuratorate, the People's Court shall accept it.

Article 414 Where the People's Procuratorate files a protest according to law against a legally effective judgment or a ruling on non-acceptance or dismissal of prosecution, the People's Court shall accept it, except for judgments or rulings that do not apply the trial supervision procedure, such as judgments or rulings applying the special procedure, summary procedure, public summons procedure, bankruptcy procedure, or divorce judgments or rulings.

Article 415 Where the People's Procuratorate, in accordance with Item (3) of paragraph 1 of Article 209 of the Civil Procedure Law, files a protest or a retrial procuratorial suggestion against a retrial judgment or ruling containing obvious errors, the People's Court shall accept it.

Article 418 After a party's retrial application has been rejected by a ruling of a higher People's Court, if the People's Procuratorate files a protest against the original judgment, ruling, or mediation document, and the grounds for the protest fall under any of the circumstances provided in Items (1) through (5) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court that accepts the protest may refer the case to the next lower People's Court for retrial.

Article 419 After receiving a retrial procuratorial suggestion, the People's Court shall form a collegial panel and conduct a review within three months. If it finds that the original judgment, ruling, or mediation document is indeed erroneous and a retrial is necessary, it shall rule to retry the case in accordance with Article 198 of the Civil Procedure Law and notify the parties; if, after review, it decides not to retry the case, it shall reply in writing to the People's Procuratorate.

Article 420 When a People's Court tries a case that has been ruled to be retried due to a protest or procuratorial suggestion from the People's Procuratorate, it shall not be affected by any previous ruling rejecting the party's retrial application.

Article 421 When a People's Court opens a court session to hear a protest case, it shall notify the People's Procuratorate, the parties, and other participants in the proceedings three days before the court session. The People's Procuratorate at the same level or the People's Procuratorate that filed the protest shall send personnel to appear in court.
Where a People's Procuratorate investigates and verifies circumstances with a party or a person not involved in the case in performing its duty of legal supervision, it shall submit such circumstances to the court and explain them, and the parties shall conduct cross-examination.

Article 422 Where a party who must participate in the joint action fails to participate in the action for reasons not attributable to itself or its authorized agent, it may, under Article 200(8) of the Civil Procedure Law, apply for retrial within six months from the date it knows or should have known of such failure, except where the circumstances provided for in Article 423 of this Interpretation apply.
Where a People's Court decides to conduct a retrial upon the application of a party as specified in the preceding paragraph, if the retrial is conducted under the procedure of first instance, the court shall add such party as a party and render a new judgment or ruling; if the retrial is conducted under the procedure of second instance, and no agreement can be reached through mediation, the court shall vacate the original judgment or ruling and remand the case for retrial, and at the retrial, such party shall be added as a party.

Article 423 Under Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, where a person not involved in the case is dissatisfied with the ruling rejecting its objection to enforcement and considers that the original judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement contains errors that harm its civil rights and interests, it may apply for retrial with the People's Court that rendered the original judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement within six months from the date the ruling on the enforcement objection is served.

Article 424 Under Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, after a People's Court decides to conduct a retrial, if the person not involved in the case is a necessary party to the joint action, the matter shall be handled in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 422 of this Interpretation.
If the person not involved in the case is not a necessary party to the joint action, the People's Court shall only hear the part of the original judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement that harms its civil rights and interests. After the hearing, if the retrial petition is sustained, the court shall vacate or modify the original judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement; if the retrial petition is not sustained, the court shall affirm the original judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement.
Article 425 The provisions of Article 340 of this Interpretation shall apply to the procedure for trial supervision.

Article 426 With respect to a judgment or ruling in a small-claim case, where a party applies for retrial with the original trial court on the grounds specified in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall accept the application. If the grounds for retrial are sustained, the court shall decide to conduct a retrial, form a collegiate panel, and hear the case. The party may not appeal against the judgment or ruling rendered on retrial.
Where a party applies for retrial with the original trial court on the ground that the case should not have been tried as a small-claim case, the People's Court shall accept the application. If the ground is sustained, the court shall decide to conduct a retrial, form a collegiate panel, and hear the case. The party may appeal against the judgment or ruling rendered on retrial.

Article 427 Where two or more People's Courts have jurisdiction, the creditor may apply for a payment order to any one of the Primary People's Courts.
Where a creditor applies for a payment order to two or more Primary People's Courts that have jurisdiction, the court that first dockets the case shall have jurisdiction.

Article 428 After receiving a creditor's application for a payment order, if the People's Court considers that the application does not comply with the requirements, it may notify the creditor to correct the application within a specified time limit. The People's Court shall notify the creditor whether the application is accepted within five days from the date of receiving the corrected materials.
Article 431 Where service of a payment order is made on the debtor himself and the debtor refuses to receive it, the People's Court may serve it by leaving it at the debtor's premises.

Article 432 Under any of the following circumstances, the People's Court shall rule to terminate the summary procedure for urging debt repayment, and if a payment order has been issued, the payment order shall automatically become invalid:
(1) After the People's Court accepts the application for a payment order, the creditor files another lawsuit on the same creditor-debtor relationship;
(2) The payment order cannot be served on the debtor within thirty days from the date it is issued by the People's Court; or
(3) The creditor withdraws the application before the debtor receives the payment order.

Article 433 Where, after receiving a payment order, the debtor fails to raise a written objection within the statutory time limit but files a lawsuit with another People's Court, the validity of the payment order shall not be affected.
If the debtor raises an objection beyond the statutory time limit, it shall be deemed that no objection has been raised.

Article 434 Where a creditor makes multiple payment claims against the debtor in the same application for a payment order based on the same creditor-debtor relationship, and the debtor raises an objection to only one or several of the claims, the validity of the other claims shall not be affected.

Article 435 Where a creditor, based on the same creditor-debtor relationship, makes payment claims against multiple debtors for a divisible obligation, and one or several of the multiple debtors raise objections, the validity of the other claims shall not be affected.

Article 436 A payment order issued against the principal debtor for a secured debt shall not be binding on the surety.
Where a creditor separately files a lawsuit on the suretyship relationship, the payment order shall become invalid from the date the People's Court accepts the case.
